summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments in 18.3 minutes, including 2 compute-bound experiments. Qwen3.8 source-grounding trace capture was the longest listed compute-bound run at 17.5 minutes, but no data available this milestone explains its phase-level cost. The task-conditioned field reports no GPU-idle compute fault, and no data available this milestone establishes concurrent loading of 2 or more models or a missed DualGPURunner dispatch.
bottlenecks_identified: Qwen3.8 source-grounding trace capture dominated the recorded wall-time window at 17.5 minutes.
Disk-mtime reconstruction has no phase boundaries, so it cannot separate setup, model loading, inference, or output work within the longest run.
The GPU snapshot is not task-correlated, which prevents a stronger efficiency diagnosis and leaves parallel-model runner eligibility unknown.
improvements_suggested: Add task-scoped monotonic timers for setup, model loading, inference, and artifact writing.
Record compute-window GPU utilization with task and process ownership instead of relying on an uncorrelated snapshot.
Emit model-count and runner-choice receipts before compute dispatch, and select DualGPURunner only for tasks that load at least two models in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument the Qwen3.8 trace path with phase-level timing.
Capture task-owned GPU telemetry throughout every compute-bound run.
Make model concurrency and runner selection explicit in each compute receipt.
meta_reflection: The evidence can rank elapsed time, but it cannot assign a cause to the dominant run. The locked compute-task idle field is false, so the separate idle snapshot is not treated as proof of wasted GPU time.
